title: The Evolution of Trust
subtitle: An interactive guide to the game theory of why and how we trust each other.
learning_goals: Distinguish zero-sum from non-zero-sum interactions, and explain why repeated non-zero-sum play creates space for cooperation that single-shot play does not.
Compare canonical iterated prisoner's dilemma strategies (Always Cooperate, Always Cheat, Tit-for-Tat, Grim Trigger, Copycat with forgiveness, Detective, etc.) in terms of when each wins and why.
Identify the structural conditions a society needs to evolve cooperation: repeat encounters, possible win-wins, and low miscommunication — and predict what happens when each is removed.
creator: Nicky Case
notes: The Evolution of Trust was created by Nicky Case (https://ncase.me) and released under a Creative Commons Zero (CC0) public domain dedication. It is based on Robert Axelrod's 1984 book *The Evolution of Cooperation*, which itself synthesises results from iterated-prisoner's-dilemma tournaments. Music 'Bleu' by Komiku, also CC0. This Galvoro capsule is a near-verbatim fork: gameplay, copy, art, animation, and audio are unchanged from upstream. Edits are limited to those required by the Galvoro Capsule Contribution Spec — namely, the removal of external social, share, donation, and translation links (which cannot function inside the Galvoro sandbox), removal of off-origin form submissions, and the addition of capsule metadata. All pedagogical and creative credit belongs to Nicky Case.
